Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
Acute systemic allergic reaction likely progressing toward anaphylaxis following wasp sting. Supporting features: symptoms began within minutes, respiratory involvement (shallow breathing, chest tightness), cutaneous findings (blotchy rash, lip tingling). No prior similar episodes; no recorded airway swelling yet but risk of rapid progression.  

Plan:  
• Immediate administration of available oral antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Wife instructed to call emergency services (ambulance) rather than self-transport.  
• Advise urgent hospital assessment for possible anaphylaxis and need for parenteral adrenaline, airway support, and observation.  
• Educated on seriousness and potential rapid deterioration.  
• No outpatient investigations appropriate at this time; emergency care prioritized.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting – High likelihood. Immediate multisystem symptoms (respiratory + cutaneous); clinician’s urgent management consistent.  
2. Systemic allergic urticaria without full anaphylaxis – Moderate likelihood. Cutaneous signs present but respiratory complaints suggest higher concern.  
3. Anxiety/panic-induced hyperventilation – Low likelihood. Respiratory symptoms could be stress related, yet allergic signs favor immunologic reaction.
